proposal_title: Security Credential Injection, Buffer Zeroing & Telemetry Redaction
domain_specific_rationale: As Red Team Specialist with mandatory sign-off authority, CP-007 replaces ambiguous cryptographic claims ('SecretEnclave') with practical, auditable, and testable defense-in-depth controls. From an adversarial penetration perspective, the primary attack surfaces in browser-based automation are memory dump extraction, accidental log harvesting, and local profile theft. By mandating OS-level credential injection at startup, immediate in-memory Buffer zeroing (buf.fill(0)), telemetry redaction of sensitive HTTP headers (Authorization, Cookie, set-cookie), and chmod 700 isolation on Chrome user profiles, this change significantly reduces secret exposure risk across all worker nodes.
capability_impact: Preserves and reinforces CAP-07 (Security & Isolation) and CAP-15 (Anti-Abuse Compliance).
residual_risk: Residual Risk: In Node.js/V8 environments, string-allocated secrets (immutable in JS) cannot be wiped by buf.fill(0) if converted to strings before zeroing, which could leave ephemeral copies in V8 heap string table. Required Mitigation: Ensure all secret ingestion and provider signing routines in R07 and R09 manipulate binary Buffer/Uint8Array directly without intermediate string conversion, and include heap inspection unit tests in the security test suite.
